newsitem.title: UK: UK retailers welcome Brown's first budget.
newsitem.headline: UK retailers welcome Brown's first budget.

text.p: British retailers, represented by the British Retail Consortium have welcomed Gordon Brown's first budget and said measures to restrain the consumer have lessened the need for further interest rate rises.
"We're welcoming the budget overall, the accent remains where it should be on tight control of public expenditure," a BRC spokesman told Reuters.
"The Chancellor has taken about one billion stg out of the consumer economy in the short-term, which we see as lessening the need for interest rate rises,' he said.
The spokesman said retailers would welcome the fact that the more siren calls for personal tax increases were ignored. "We did not think that was necessary," he said.
The BRC was less happy about the increase of duties but gratefully. "But we appreciate being given plenty of notice," he said.

In the first Labour budget in nearly 20 years, Brown told parliament he would raise tobacco duties by a further two percent points but not until December 1. Alcohol duties would rise by inflation only from January.
